hook.text: An ant can carry 50 times its body weight. Scale it to human size and its legs would snap from its own mass.

buildup.text: Scaling laws say things change in unexpected ways as they grow. What works small often fails at scale.

discovery.text: A startup with five people needs no process. At five hundred, the same approach causes chaos. Structure must scale.

twist.text: Some things scale beautifully. Software costs nearly nothing to give to one more user. A restaurant cannot do that.

climax.text: Always ask: does this approach scale? What breaks first as the numbers grow? Address that bottleneck early.

punchline.text: What works small often breaks big. Plan for scale early.

quiz.question: What do scaling laws teach about growth?
options: Properties change in unexpected ways as size increases
